# Bending Spoons’ Bold $1.28 Billion Move to Own Airtable  
Bending Spoons just made a massive splash. On August 4, 2026, the company announced it will acquire Airtable in a deal valued at $1.28 billion in cash. This isn’t just another buyout. It’s a game-changer for both companies and the software world at large.
## Why Bending Spoons? Why Now?  
Bending Spoons, fresh off its July 2026 public debut at an $18 billion valuation, is on a mission. It’s no stranger to big acquisitions, having added Evernote, WeTransfer, EventBrite, and Vimeo to its portfolio. But this marks its first acquisition since going public.  
The deal means Bending Spoons will buy all issued and outstanding shares of Airtable for $1.28 billion in cash. It’s a bold bet on Airtable’s future and its growing revenue.  
Airtable’s annual recurring revenue jumped over 20% year-on-year to about $480 million by June 2026. Luca Ferrari, CEO and co-founder of Bending Spoons, emphasized this growth: “The value being delivered is reflected in annual recurring revenue growing over 20% YoY to approximately $480m as of June 2026, and joining forces with Bending Spoons will accelerate innovation even further.”  
Ferrari also pointed to Airtable’s pioneering role: “We’re looking forward to welcoming Airtable into Bending Spoons. Airtable is a pioneering brand reshaping how teams organise data and manage critical workflows.”
## What’s Next for Airtable and Bending Spoons?  
Airtable has been innovating beyond spreadsheets and databases. Earlier in 2026, it launched a new product line under the Superagent name. This shows the company’s push toward more advanced, AI-driven tools.  
The acquisition promises to fuel these innovations further. Howie Liu sees Bending Spoons as the perfect partner: “Partnering with Bending Spoons gives us the resources and the long-term commitment Airtable needs to pursue that vision even more boldly as we build the AI-native platform of the future.”  
With Bending Spoons’ deep pockets and strategic vision, Airtable could accelerate its AI-native ambitions. This deal is not just about ownership. It’s about joining forces to redefine how teams work and innovate with data.  
Keep an eye on this space. The combined power of Bending Spoons and Airtable could reshape workflows for millions. The future of work just got a major upgrade.

results.content:
**MILAN, Italy, August 4, 2026** — [Bending Spoons](https://bendingspoons.com/) S.p.A. has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire Airtable in an all-cash transaction that values the enterprise software company at an enterprise value of $1.285 billion. When Airtable's current net cash and cash equivalents are included, the transaction implies an equity value of approximately $2.25 billion. The acquisition has been unanimously approved by the boards of directors of both companies and remains subject to regulatory approvals and other closing requirements. The companies expect the transaction to close later this year, while Bending Spoons and Airtable will continue operating independently until the deal is finalized.  
The proposed acquisition represents Bending Spoons' first announced transaction since completing its Nasdaq listing on July 1, 2026, marking another milestone in the company's acquisition strategy. By adding Airtable to its portfolio, Bending Spoons expands its presence in enterprise software with a company that has established a significant global customer base and recurring subscription business. The agreement also reflects ongoing consolidation within the software sector, where companies with established enterprise platforms and recurring revenue continue to attract strategic buyers.  
**Expanding an Acquisition Portfolio**
**Expanding an Acquisition Portfolio**  
The [Airtable](https://www.airtable.com/) transaction follows a series of acquisitions completed by Bending Spoons over the past several years. Earlier in 2026, the company acquired AOL in January and Eventbrite in March, adding to a portfolio that already includes Brightcove, Evernote, Harvest, komoot, Remini, StreamYard, Vimeo, and WeTransfer. As of March 2026, Bending Spoons reported serving more than 500 million monthly active users and over 9 million monthly paying customers across its portfolio of applications and digital platforms.  
Bending Spoons has built its business around acquiring established digital companies and investing in product development, technology, organizational restructuring, user experience, marketing, and monetization initiatives designed to expand long-term earnings. According to the company, it has executed this acquisition strategy for more than a decade and has never sold a material business. It also stated that artificial intelligence plays an important role in both its long-term vision for acquired businesses and the technologies it develops across its portfolio.  
**Airtable’s Growth Story**
Image credit: Airtable  
**Transaction Structure and Advisors**  
Under the terms of the agreement, unanimously approved by the boards of directors of both companies, Bending Spoons will acquire 100% of Airtable’s issued and outstanding shares through an all-cash transaction. Completion of the acquisition remains subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing requirements, and both companies will continue conducting business independently until the transaction is completed. The proposed deal expands Bending Spoons’ [enterprise software](https://smebusinessreview.com/magazine/2026/10-fast-growing-enterprise-software-companies-to-watch-2026) portfolio with one of the world’s largest no-code application platforms while adding another globally recognized technology brand to its collection of digital businesses.

The most valuable no-code company of the last decade just changed hands for a number that would have been unthinkable five years ago. On August 4, 2026, Bending Spoons agreed to acquire Airtable for US$1.285 billion in an all-cash deal, a staggering drop from the US$11.7 billion valuation Airtable commanded at the peak of the 2021 software boom. For anyone tracking where enterprise software is heading, this is not just a headline about one company. It is a signal about how the ground has shifted under the entire SaaS industry.
Bending Spoons paid an enterprise value of US$1.285 billion, with an implied equity value closer to US$2.25 billion once Airtable's net cash is included. Luca Ferrari, Bending Spoons' CEO, called Airtable "a pioneering brand reshaping how teams organize data and manage critical workflows." Airtable co-founder and CEO Howie Liu noted that "more than 500,000 organizations rely on Airtable to power their most critical work."
## Who is Bending Spoons  
If the buyer's name is unfamiliar, the apps it owns are not. Bending Spoons is the Italian company that has quietly assembled a portfolio of well-known consumer and productivity brands: Evernote, Vimeo, WeTransfer, Brightcove, Eventbrite, Harvest, StreamYard, komoot, Remini, and even AOL. As of March 2026, its products reached more than 500 million monthly active users and over 9 million paying customers. Airtable is its first acquisition since going public on the Nasdaq on July 1, 2026.  
Bending Spoons has a well-earned reputation for buying mature software companies, running them efficiently, and prioritizing profit over hypergrowth. The company says it plans to invest in Airtable's core strengths for the long term and expand its functionality, with AI capabilities as part of the transformation. The all-cash deal was unanimously approved by both boards and is expected to close later in 2026, pending regulatory approval.

In Brief  
Posted:  
4:30 AM PDT · August 4, 2026  
In its first acquisition since going public last month, Bending Spoons on Tuesday said that it has agreed to buy spreadsheet and database startup Airtable for $1.28 billion in cash.  
Founded in 2013, Airtable has so far raised over $1.4 billion over multiple funding rounds. At its peak, during the boom days of 2021, it was valued at over $11 billion, but earlier this year, its shares were said to be [trading on the secondary markets at a valuation of $4 billion](https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/27/airtables-valuation-fell-by-7-million-its-founder-thinks-that-was-just-the-warm-up/).  
With its current net cash-and-cash-equivalents balance, Airtable is now valued at about $2.25 billion, Bending Spoons said.  
“Airtable is a pioneering brand reshaping how teams organize data and manage critical workflows. The value being delivered is reflected in annual recurring revenue growing over 20% YoY to approximately $480 million as of June 2026, and joining forces with Bending Spoons will accelerate innovation even further,” Bending Spoons’ founder Luca Ferrrai said in a statement.
In January, Airtable unveiled [a new product line](https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/27/airtables-valuation-fell-by-7-million-its-founder-thinks-that-was-just-the-warm-up/) under the Superagent moniker: an orchestration platform that can help users spin up a team of AI agents to do tasks. The company’s CEO, Howie Liu, said at the time that Airtable serves over 500,000 organizations, including 80% of the Fortune 100.  
Bending Spoons, which went public at [an $18 billion valuation in July](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/01/after-18b-ipo-bending-spoons-founder-says-success-comes-from-minimizing-luck/), typically acquires companies that are trading at a decent discount to their private valuations, trims the staff, streamlines products, and tries to make them run profitably.  
The company has so far acquired several notable brands, including Evernote, [WeTransfer](https://techcrunch.com/2024/07/31/bending-spoons-acquires-file-transfer-service-wetransfer/), [EventBrite](https://techcrunch.com/2024/07/31/bending-spoons-acquires-file-transfer-service-wetransfer/) and [Vimeo](https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/08/eventbrite-and-vimeo-owner-bending-spoons-files-to-go-public/).

August 5, 2026, 3:07 PM ET · Italian unicorn Bending Spoons made its first acquisition since going public.Michael Nagle—Bloomberg/Getty Images · Add Fortune on Google for similar content.Add us on GoogleAdd us on Google · Bending Spoons, the former unicorn that posted 95% revenue growth year over year, agreed Tuesday to buy Airtable in an all-cash deal that values the software company at $1.285 billion, with an equity value of about $2.25 billion once Airtable’s cash balance is factored in. That momentum continued into 2026, with first-quarter revenue more than doubling to $601.3 million and the company swinging to a $27.5 million net profit from a $112.2 million net loss a year earlier. Bending Spoons priced its Nasdaq listing at $29 a share in July, above its marketed range, valuing the company at roughly $18.4 billion; shares closed at $36.22 on Monday.
